name: UK inflation & rates
summary: UK CPI rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%; Bank Rate 4% with markets pricing about an 80% chance of a December rise
state: The ONS reported on 18 Nov that CPI rose 3.6% in the 12 months to October, up from 3.5% and just below the 3.7% forecast, with motor fuels the largest upward driver (ONS; ITV News). That sits inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band. After the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% in November, markets price about an 80% chance of another rise in December (Trading Economics).
for_you: Higher inflation and rate rises push up costs for borrowers on variable or expiring fixed-rate mortgages, while savings rates tend to follow Bank Rate.
rubric_hit: Watch: CPI 3.6% within the 2.5–4.0% band (ONS, Oct)

why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
